name: surrogate
title: A permutation, a phase surrogate, and an amplitude surrogate. The phase draw is runif and the normal draw is R's two-uniform rnorm. The inverse FFT is not divided by n.

origin.description: A permutation, a phase surrogate, and an amplitude surrogate. The phase draw is runif and the normal draw is R's two-uniform rnorm. The inverse FFT is not divided by n.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The series, matrix, or path this function accepts.

origin.details: A permutation, a phase surrogate, and an amplitude surrogate. The phase draw is runif and the normal draw is R's two-uniform rnorm. The inverse FFT is not divided by n.
origin.value: The same value tseries 0.10-63 returns for this case, written as one line.
origin.example:
z <- sin((1:8)/3)
set.seed(1); a <- surrogate(z, fft = FALSE)
set.seed(1); b <- surrogate(z, fft = TRUE)
set.seed(1); c <- surrogate(z, fft = TRUE, amplitude = TRUE)
set.seed(4); d <- surrogate(sin((1:10)/3), ns = 2, statistic = function(v) v[1])
paste(join(a), join(b), join(c), cell(d$orig.statistic), cell(d$bias), join(d$statistic), sep = "|")

translation.description: A permutation, a phase surrogate, and an amplitude surrogate. The phase draw is runif and the normal draw is R's two-uniform rnorm. The inverse FFT is not divided by n.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The series, matrix, or path this function accepts.

translation.details: A permutation, a phase surrogate, and an amplitude surrogate. The phase draw is runif and the normal draw is R's two-uniform rnorm. The inverse FFT is not divided by n.
translation.value: The same value tseries 0.10-63 returns for this case, written as one line.
translation.example:
z = np.array([math.sin(i / 3) for i in range(1, 9)])
set_seed(1); a = surrogate(z, fft=False)
set_seed(1); b = surrogate(z, fft=True)
set_seed(1); c = surrogate(z, fft=True, amplitude=True)
set_seed(4); d = surrogate(np.array([math.sin(i / 3) for i in range(1, 11)]), ns=2, statistic=lambda v: v[0])
return "|".join([join(a), join(b), join(c), cell(float(np.ravel(d["orig_statistic"])[0])), cell(float(np.ravel(d["bias"])[0])), join(d["statistic"])])
